current_example.problem: Given that $X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.3)$ and $Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7)$ are independent, calculate $P(X=0 \, \cup \, Y=0).$
current_example.worked_solution:
By the addition law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)+P(Y=0)-P(X=0\,\cap \,Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplication law for independent events, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cap \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)+P(Y=0)-P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $X\sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.3),$ we have

$$
P(X=1) = 0.3, \quad P(X=0) = 0.7,
$$

and since $Y \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(0.7),$ we have

$$
P(Y=1)=0.7, \quad P(Y=0)=0.3.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=0\,\cup \,Y=0) & =P(X=0)+P(Y=0)-P(X=0)\cdot P(Y=0) \\  & =0.7+0.3-0.7\cdot 0.3 \\  & =1-0.21 \\  & =0.79.\end{aligned}
$$
